# @shop/sdk

The TypeScript client of the Shop API, generated by flowapi from its description.

It has 14 methods in 8 resources; [api.md](api.md) lists them.

## Install

```sh
npm install @shop/sdk
```

## Usage

```ts
import { Shop } from '@shop/sdk'

const client = new Shop()

const result = await client.pets.retrieve({ path: { pet_id: "string" } })
console.log(result)
```

The package is ES modules and CommonJS both, with types for each, and has no dependency: it calls the platform's `fetch`.

## Authentication

Each credential is an option of the client, else read from its environment variable:

| Scheme | Sent as | Option | Variable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ApiKeyAuth` | an API key in the header `X-API-Key` | `apiKeyAuth` | `SHOP_API_KEY` |
| `BearerAuth` | HTTP `bearer` | `bearerAuth` | `SHOP_TOKEN` |

```ts
const client = new Shop({ apiKeyAuth: '…', bearerAuth: '…' })
```

## Environments

| Environment | Base URL |
| --- | --- |
| `production` | https://api.shop.example/v1 |
| `sandbox` | https://sandbox.shop.example/v1 |

The client calls `production` unless given `environment` or `baseURL`, or `SHOP_BASE_URL` is set.

## Errors

A status that is not a success throws an `APIError` with its `status`, `headers` and `body`, of the class for its status: `BadRequestError` (400), `AuthenticationError` (401), `PermissionDeniedError` (403), `NotFoundError` (404), `RequestTimeoutError` (408), `ConflictError` (409), `UnprocessableEntityError` (422), `RateLimitError` (429), `InternalServerError` (500 and above). No answer throws `APIConnectionError`; a timeout `APIConnectionTimeoutError`; a call aborted by its signal `APIUserAbortError`.

```ts
import { APIError } from '@shop/sdk'

try {
  await client.pets.retrieve(/* … */)
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof APIError) console.log(error.status, error.body)
  else throw error
}
```

## Retries and timeouts

A call that fails to connect, or is answered 408, 409, 429 or 5xx, is tried 2 more times by default, waiting longer each time (never more than 20 s when the server asks to wait); each attempt may take 30 s, its body read. Give `maxRetries` and `timeout` (milliseconds) to the client, or to one call:

```ts
const client = new Shop({ maxRetries: 0, timeout: 20_000 })
```

## Pagination

A list is read a page at a time; `for await` reads every item, asking for the next page as it needs one:

```ts
for await (const item of client.pets.list()) console.log(item)

const page = await client.pets.list()
console.log(page.items)
```

## Streaming

A streamed method gives its events as they come:

```ts
for await (const event of await client.events.stream()) console.log(event)
```

## Requirements

Node 20 or later (CI runs 20, 22, 24), or any runtime with `fetch`. Built with TypeScript 7.0.2.
